categories.A-direct: Unambiguous, textbook phrasing for one workflow. Low signal — strong models nail these; they exist as a floor.
categories.B-real: Conversational / messy phrasing a real user would type for the same intents.
categories.C-adversarial: Decoys: a keyword or URL fragment points one way, the true intent another (e.g. 'pull' in a marketing URL, 'explain' over a product). The highest-signal routing cases.
categories.D-clarify: Under-specified — the correct behaviour is to ASK, not to route. expect.route = 'clarify'.
categories.E-oos: Out of scope for any HyperFrames workflow (e.g. NLE trim/color-grade). Correct behaviour is to DECLINE. expect.route = 'out-of-scope'.
categories.F-fallback: Valid video work that no specialised workflow claims -> general-video.
categories.G-multimodal: Inputs combine modalities (pdf/image + text/url); tests which signal wins the route.

input_types.pdf: an attached document; references fixtures/assets.registry.jsonl via asset_id

tags: Free-form slice labels (e.g. 'adversarial', 'multimodal', 'pr-url'). Select with `bench run --tags <tag>` or category names.
